implementation_statement: An access control policy existed only as a 2021 section of the information security program. POL-02 (P06), approved 2026-08-27, replaces it. WDBP access procedures for the admin console and wire platform are due 2026-11-30.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider; identity provider
implementation_statement: Workforce accounts for the online banking admin console and the wire platform are created from HR tickets and federated through the identity provider. Business customer users are created by the Treasury Management Officer under each customer's agreement. Gap: no quarterly review of admin console and wire platform entitlements; departed employees are disabled within 1 to 3 business days rather than the same day.
evidence: Onboarding tickets; admin console user export; wire platform user list

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Role-based access in the wire platform separates wire entry, wire approval, and template maintenance roles. The admin console has help-desk, treasury, and administrator roles. Business users receive entitlements set by the customer's administrator within bank-set limits.
evidence: Wire platform role matrix; admin console role export

implementation_statement: Maker-checker is enforced for every outgoing wire: the person who keys a wire cannot approve it. Gap: the 2 wire approvers can also create and edit beneficiary templates, so template changes are not independently reviewed (R-019).
Standard users have no local administrator rights on wire-room and branch endpoints. Gap: 3 IT staff hold full administrator rights in the admin console for day-to-day help-desk work.
evidence: Endpoint policy; admin console role export

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; identity provider
implementation_statement: The identity provider locks workforce accounts for 15 minutes after 10 failed attempts. The digital banking provider locks customer logons after 5 failed attempts and requires a reset through the help desk or out-of-band verification.
Wire-room and branch workstations lock after 5 minutes idle (teller and payments workstations) or 10 minutes (other endpoints), enforced by device management.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Customer online banking sessions end after 10 minutes idle; admin console and wire platform sessions after 15 minutes (provider settings confirmed).
Remote access to the WDBP admin functions is allowed only through the identity provider with MFA from bank-managed laptops. The payments workstations cannot be reached remotely.
Awareness and training requirements are in POL-05 (P06), approved 2026-08-27.
Annual security awareness training and two phishing simulations a year for all staff. Gap: content does not cover payment-fraud and BEC red flags for branch staff.
Planned: role-based wire-fraud and callback training for branch managers, universal bankers, and wire-room staff by 2026-11-30 (R-026).

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider; identity provider
implementation_statement: The admin console, wire platform, and identity provider log sign-ins, entitlement changes, beneficiary and limit changes, and wire events by default.

provider_if_inherited: Payments service provider
implementation_statement: Wire platform audit records include user, role, action, wire reference, amount, beneficiary, timestamp, and workstation.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: admin console and wire platform audit logs are not reviewed. Planned: a daily exception report of beneficiary, template, and limit changes reviewed by Deposit Operations, and forwarding of logs to the MSSP, starting 2026-11 (R-009).

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Providers retain audit logs for the contract term. Gap: identity provider logs use the default 30-day retention; export to the central log archive (SYS-06) is planned.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Audit record generation is enabled by default in both vendor-hosted services and cannot be turned off by bank users.
Control assessment performed 2026-08-03 to 2026-08-07 by an independent assessor (P07). The annual IT audit by outsourced internal audit also tests wire controls.
Weaknesses are tracked in the P07 POA&M with owners and dates and reported to the Audit and Risk Committee quarterly.
Planned: monthly metrics (callback compliance, customer MFA enrollment, open POA&M items) reported to the COO, and quarterly to the Audit and Risk Committee.

The two payments workstations are built from a documented hardened image. Gap: no documented baseline for the admin console and wire platform configuration settings the bank controls (limits, dual-approval thresholds, callback fields).
Changes to the payments workstations go through the IT change log. Gap: changes to wire limits and dual-approval thresholds in the admin console are made by email request without a change record.
Endpoint settings are enforced by device management. Gap: the admin console security settings (customer MFA, beneficiary confirmation) are left at provider defaults, which make MFA optional.
evidence: Device management report; admin console settings

implementation_statement: Payments workstations run only the browser and token software needed for the wire platform and the Federal Reserve payment services; email and general browsing are blocked.
All WDBP endpoints, including the 2 payments workstations and the 5 wire-room PCs, are in the device inventory with location and owner.
The business continuity plan (2025) includes contingency planning policy for payments.

provider_if_inherited: Payments service provider; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: The business continuity plan includes an alternate wire procedure and provider recovery commitments. Gap: it does not use the BIA recovery objectives (P05) or name an alternate site for the wire room.
Gap: the alternate wire procedure has not been tested since 2023. Planned: semiannual test with a live low-value wire, first on 2026-11-12 (R-010).

provider_if_inherited: Payments service provider; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Providers back up wire, customer, and configuration data. The bank exports wire platform configuration monthly to the backup vault. Gap: the vault is in the same cloud account as production and is not immutable.

provider_if_inherited: Payments service provider; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Recovery of the vendor-hosted services is the providers' responsibility per their SOC 2 reports. Bank-side recovery of payments workstations uses a spare pre-built workstation at Branch 4.
evidence: Provider SOC 2 reports; spare device record

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider
implementation_statement: All workforce users authenticate with unique IDs through the identity provider. Payments workstation users also use a hardware token for the Federal Reserve payment services.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider
implementation_statement: MFA is required for all privileged accounts on the admin console, wire platform, and cloud console. Administrators use phishing-resistant hardware keys.

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider
implementation_statement: MFA is required for all workforce access to the WDBP. Gap: push approval without number matching is allowed for non-privileged users (R-013).

provider_if_inherited: Identity provider; digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Workforce password length (14) and banned-password list are enforced. Customer passwords follow the provider's policy (minimum 10 characters). Gap: customer password resets by phone rely on knowledge questions.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider
implementation_statement: Customers authenticate to online and mobile banking with a user ID, password, and device recognition. Gap: MFA is optional; 31% of consumer users and 58% of business users have enabled it, and password-only business users can add wire beneficiaries (R-002).
POL-03 Incident Response Policy approved 2026-08-27 (P06).
The 2023 incident response plan covers containment and escalation. The BEC and fraudulent wire runbook (P08) was approved 2026-08-31. Gap: tabletop exercise not yet held (due 2026-11-30).
Fraud cases are tracked in the BSA case system. Gap: security incidents are not tracked in one log with the fraud cases they cause.

SAR filing and law enforcement contacts are established. Gap: the plan lacks the 36-hour OCC notification step and its determination criteria (12 CFR 53.3) and the Federal Reserve notice for the holding company (12 CFR 225.302). Added in the P08 runbook; plan update due 2026-10-31.
Incident response plan elements are in POL-03 and the P08 runbook. The 2023 plan is being rewritten to match.
The wire room is badge-controlled with an access list of 9 people; payments workstations are in the wire room only.
The five-policy set (P06) was approved by the Audit and Risk Committee on 2026-08-27, with an annual review cycle.
This SSP.
POL-05 Acceptable Use approved 2026-08-27. Staff acknowledgments due 2026-10-31.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The written information security program approved by the board in November 2025 and this policy set form the program plan. The board re-approves the updated program on 2026-10-15.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The IT Manager is designated ISO by board resolution. Gap: limited independence, because the ISO also runs IT operations and reports to the COO (R-020).

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: Risk acceptance levels are in POL-01 and the P01 register. Gap: no board-approved risk appetite (R-008); adoption scheduled 2026-10-15.
Background checks, including criminal history, are completed for all hires before start.
HR emails IT at termination. Gap: no same-day disable requirement for WDBP access; 1 to 3 business day lag observed.
Annual risk assessment (December 2025) and the 2026 register (P01, SP 800-30 Rev. 1). Gap: not tied to a board-approved risk appetite.
Annual external penetration test covers the internet-facing perimeter. Gap: no routine authenticated scanning of payments and branch endpoints; monthly MSSP scans start 2026-11 (R-021).
Critical processes and their dependencies are identified in the BIA (P05).
Security and confidentiality provisions are in the digital banking and payments service contracts. Gap: no incident notice time frame, no 12 CFR 53.4 contact, and no right to bridge letters.
Due diligence was performed at selection (2019 and 2021). SOC 2 reports are collected annually. Gap: reports are not reviewed and CUECs are not mapped to bank controls (P09).
Payments workstations sit on an isolated network segment that can reach only the wire platform and the Federal Reserve payment services. Branch firewalls allow no inbound services.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: TLS 1.2 or higher for online banking, the admin console, and the wire platform; private circuits and IPsec to the core processor.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Providers use validated cryptographic modules per their SOC 2 system descriptions.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; payments service provider
implementation_statement: Providers encrypt customer and wire data at rest. Laptops use full-disk encryption; payments workstations store no wire data locally.
Operating system patches install automatically on WDBP endpoints within 14 days. Gap: branch firewall firmware is updated quarterly rather than on a risk basis.
EDR on every WDBP endpoint, monitored 24x7 by the MSSP.

provider_if_inherited: Digital banking provider; MSSP
implementation_statement: The MSSP monitors endpoint and firewall alerts. The provider scores customer logins for fraud. Gap: no alerting on new wire beneficiaries or limit changes, and no review of the provider's fraud alerts outside business hours.
evidence: MSSP monthly report; provider fraud alert queue

implementation_statement: Planned: documented annual review of SOC reports for critical providers, starting with the core processor (completed 2026-08-20, P09), then the digital banking and payments service providers by 2026-11-30.
